title: The 86% habit of couples who last
lines: Can a *bird* tell if you two will last?
Bo, look. A bird!
That was a *bid*, Pip. A tiny ask for my attention.
And you looked up. So?
Newlyweds were watched for exactly this. Those still married years later turned toward bids *86 percent* of the time.
And the ones who divorced?
*33 percent.*
So I should point at more birds.
Be honest: do you look up?

title: What holding hands does to your brain
lines: Whose hand calms your brain *the most*?
Depends who is holding it.
A hand is a hand.
Married women were told a small shock might come. Alone, their brains braced for it.
And holding a stranger's hand?
Not as much. Their husband's hand calmed the brain *the most*.
And the happier the couple, the *calmer* it stayed.
Okay. Give me your hand.
Scared? Their hand, or your own?

title: Do couples really start to look alike?
lines: Do couples really start to *look alike*?
Everyone says so. Grow old together, end up twins.
A famous study agreed with you.
Told you.
Then photos of *517 couples* were compared, early on and 20 to 69 years later.
They did *not* grow more alike.
So why do old couples match?
They looked similar *from the very start*.
So, do you two look alike?
